Mole Poblano with Rice

Served at: Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe

Serves 6-8Prep 1 hour 30 minutesCook 2 hours 30 minutes

Mole Poblano is a rich, complex sauce, considered one of Mexico's national dishes. For the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe on December 12th, it is a beloved centerpiece, symbolizing celebration and gratitude, often served after mass as families gather to honor the Virgin Mary. Its deep, layered flavors make it a fitting dish for such a significant and joyous occasion.

Ingredients

  • 3-4 pounds (1.4-1.8 kg) bone-in, skin-on chicken pieces (thighs, drumsticks, breasts)
  • 1/2 white onion, quartered (for chicken broth)
  • 2 cloves garlic, smashed (for chicken broth)
  • 1 bay leaf
  • Salt to taste (for chicken and mole)
  • 4 ancho chiles (dried poblano peppers), stemmed and seeded
  • 3 mulato chiles (dried poblano peppers), stemmed and seeded
  • 3 pasilla chiles (dried pasilla negro peppers), stemmed and seeded
  • 1 chipotle chile (dried smoked jalapeño), stemmed and seeded (optional, for heat)
  • 1/4 cup (30 g) raw peanuts
  • 1/4 cup (30 g) blanched almonds
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) sesame seeds, plus more for garnish
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) pumpkin seeds (pepitas)
  • 1 (3-inch / 7.5 cm) cinnamon stick, preferably Mexican canela
  • 1/2 teaspoon whole cloves
  • 1/2 teaspoon black peppercorns
  • 1/4 teaspoon anise seeds
  • 1/2 teaspoon dried Mexican oregano
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground cumin
  • 1/2 medium white onion, roughly chopped (for mole)
  • 4 cloves garlic, peeled (for mole)
  • 2 Roma tomatoes (about 8 oz / 225 g), roughly chopped
  • 2 tomatillos (about 4 oz / 115 g), husked and roughly chopped
  • 1/2 plantain, ripe (yellow with black spots), peeled and sliced
  • 1 slice stale bread or 1 stale corn tortilla
  • 1 ounce (28 g) Mexican chocolate (unsweetened or semi-sweet), broken into pieces
  • 1 teaspoon sugar (optional, to taste)
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) lard or vegetable oil, plus 1 tablespoon (15 ml) for rice
  • 4-6 cups (960 ml - 1.4 L) chicken broth, divided (from cooking chicken)
  • 2 cups (400 g) long-grain white rice, rinsed
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) vegetable oil (for rice)
  • 1/4 cup (35 g) finely diced white onion (for rice)
  • 1 clove garlic, minced (for rice)
  • 3 cups (720 ml) chicken broth or water (for rice)
  • 1 tablespoon (15 g) tomato paste (optional, for color in rice)

Method

  1. Prepare the Chicken: Place chicken pieces, 1/2 quartered onion, 2 smashed garlic cloves, bay leaf, and a generous pinch of salt in a large pot. Cover with water by about 1 inch (2.5 cm). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through. Remove chicken, let cool slightly, then shred or cut into serving pieces. Strain the broth and reserve 4-6 cups (960 ml - 1.4 L) for the mole and rice.
  2. Prepare the Chiles: While chicken cooks, toast the dried chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat for 30-60 seconds per side, until fragrant and slightly pliable (do not burn). Transfer to a bowl, cover with hot water, and let rehydrate for 20-30 minutes until soft. Drain, reserving a little soaking liquid if needed for blending.
  3. Toast Nuts and Seeds: In the same dry skillet, toast peanuts, almonds, sesame seeds, and pumpkin seeds separately until lightly golden and fragrant. Set aside.
  4. Fry Aromatics and Spices: Heat 1/4 cup (60 ml) lard or oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the 1/2 roughly chopped onion, 4 peeled garlic cloves, tomatoes, tomatillos, plantain, and stale bread/tortilla. Fry until softened and lightly browned, about 8-10 minutes. Add the cinnamon stick, cloves, peppercorns, anise seeds, oregano, and cumin; cook for another minute until fragrant.
  5. Blend the Mole Paste: Transfer the fried aromatics, spices, toasted nuts, and rehydrated chiles to a blender. Add 2 cups (480 ml) of the reserved chicken broth. Blend until very smooth. This may take several minutes and you might need to do it in batches. For an extra smooth mole, pass the blended mixture through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids with a spoon.
  6. Cook the Mole: In the same pot (cleaned if necessary), heat another tablespoon of lard or oil over medium heat. Pour in the blended mole paste. Cook, stirring constantly, for 20-30 minutes. The mole will darken in color, thicken, and the oil will separate slightly. This step is crucial for developing deep flavor.
  7. Simmer the Mole: Gradually stir in the remaining 2-4 cups (480 ml - 960 ml) of chicken broth, a little at a time, until the mole reaches your desired consistency (it should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon). Add the Mexican chocolate and stir until melted and fully incorporated. Add the optional sugar if needed to balance the flavors. Season with salt to taste. Reduce heat to low and simmer for at least 30-60 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking, allowing the flavors to meld.
  8. Prepare the Rice: While the mole simmers, heat 1 tablespoon (15 ml) vegetable oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the rinsed rice and sauté for 3-5 minutes until lightly golden. Add the 1/4 cup (35 g) finely diced onion and minced garlic; sauté for 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
  9. Cook the Rice: Stir in 3 cups (720 ml) chicken broth (or water), optional tomato paste, and salt to taste. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until all liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes before fluffing with a fork.
  10. Serve: Add the cooked chicken pieces to the simmering mole and heat through for 5-10 minutes. Serve the Mole Poblano over chicken, accompanied by the Mexican rice. Garnish with a sprinkle of sesame seeds.

Tips

  • Make Ahead: Mole poblano tastes even better the next day! Prepare the mole sauce a day or two in advance and gently reheat, adding a little more broth if needed to adjust consistency.
  • Spice Level: Adjust the number of chipotle chiles (or omit) based on your preferred spice level. For a milder mole, remove more seeds and veins from the chiles.
  • Authenticity: Using Mexican chocolate (often found in disc or tablet form) and Mexican oregano will give your mole a more authentic flavor profile.
